title: Cervical Screening: What You Need to Know
excerpt: The National Cervical Screening Program has changed. Find out about the updated Cervical Screening Test, who it's for, and how to book at Morley GP.
body: Australia's cervical screening program changed in 2017 — the new Cervical Screening Test (CST) replaced the old Pap smear. The CST tests for human papillomavirus (HPV), which causes almost all cervical cancers. Women aged 25–74 who have ever been sexually active should have a CST every 5 years (compared to Pap smears every 2 years). The test is simple, quick, and more accurate than the previous test. If you're due for a cervical screen or have questions, book an appointment with one of our female GPs at Morley General Practice.
